FY25.dep_amort_note: Rice reports ONE combined operating line 'Depreciation and amortization'; the value is entered under 'depreciation' and 'amortization' is null because it is not separated. The cash flow statement shows the same amount as 'Depreciation of property and equipment' (FY25 82,255; FY24 81,932), so amortization is at most immaterial. Interest line is 'Interest and bond costs'.

entities_included.other: Statements consolidate 'all academic and administrative departments of the University and affiliated organizations that are controlled by the University' (Note 1, FY25 PDF p8). No hospital/health system and no FFRDC appears in the statements. Operating expenses are also shown by function (Note 14): FY25 academic programs & research 718,958; auxiliary enterprises 97,291; general administration 243,301; fundraising 28,387 ($ thousands).

calibration_fy23.explanation: S&W matches the original analysis exactly (421,781 thousand = 'Salaries and wages', benefits excluded). The reference 'core operating expenses' (959,377 thousand) equals Rice's reported TOTAL operating expenses for FY23 to the dollar, i.e. the original analysis did NOT remove depreciation & amortization (78,849) or interest (39,338). Under the SPEC definition (total - dep/amort - interest) FY23 core is 841,190 thousand, 12.3% below the reference. Definitional difference only; extraction not adjusted.

student_counts_in_official_docs: None found: the FY23-FY25 audited financial statements contain no enrollment/headcount (searched text for enrollment, students, headcount). Only dollar amounts of student aid appear (e.g., Note 11).
caveats: FY24 restatement: the FY25 report shows FY24 total operating expenses of 1,053,413 (Scholarships 73,242) and operating revenues of 1,117,047, versus 1,052,827 (Scholarships 72,656) and 1,116,461 in the FY24 report as issued; +586 on both sides, net operating income unchanged at 63,634. S&W (466,056), benefits (109,471), D&A (81,932) and interest (40,922) are identical in both. The FY25 report also states 'management revised its functional expense presentation approach' and reclassified 2024 (Note 14, PDF p25).

FY25 Scholarships expense fell to 35,543 from 73,242 while 'scholarship and fellowship awards applied to tuition and fees' (contra-revenue; student financial aid note, FY25 PDF p24) rose to 240,007 from 179,971 (FY24 report as issued: 187,565) and net tuition revenue fell to 280,603 from 294,027: a change in how aid is split between contra-revenue and expense. This makes FY25 total operating expenses and core opex not strictly comparable with FY24 (aid-related expense presentation shifted); S&W is unaffected.
FY25 S&W rose 10.7% (515,800 vs 466,056) and benefits 12.7%; taken as reported, no explanation given in the notes I read. Worth a sanity check if this growth looks too large for the leadership slide.
FY24 report debt note says interest and bond costs charged to operations were $37,853 for 2024, but the face of the FY24 statement, the FY25 statement and the FY25 note all show 40,922; 40,922 used.
'Depreciation and amortization' is a single combined line; amortization not separable.
All amounts in the source are $ thousands; the JSON is converted to whole dollars (x1,000).
